task.description:
Queue task 692 (issue). Read docs/issues/ISS-0692.yaml in full for the complete finding -- do not rely on this summary. SECURITY-REVIEWER flagged, during REQ-362's Step 2c gate, that the visual-regression-testing design (lib/letflow/design/req362-visual-regression-testing.md) commits UAT screenshot baselines to git (test/fixtures/uat/visual-baselines/), with superseded baselines retained forever in git history, and the design states zero PII/redaction/synthetic-data policy. REQ-362 itself only exercises an unauthenticated static page, so nothing in REQ-362's own diff currently violates an invariant -- the gap is that a FUTURE requirement pointing this mechanism at a real authenticated gui_screen UAT scenario (explicitly deferred per the design's own OQ-4/2.4/3.6/4.4) would have no guardrail preventing real tenant PII (candidate names, emails, etc.) from becoming a permanently git-committed artifact.

Step 0.5 (registry lookup): check docs/issues/*.yaml for a prior resolved entry about PII handling in committed test fixtures/artifacts. Note any match (or none) in your result.summary.

Step 1 (diagnose): this is a design-gap issue, not a code defect -- there is no failing test to run. Your diagnosis must state: (a) exactly which design sections need to change and what they must say (synthetic/seeded-data requirement, a redaction step, or an explicit accepted-risk statement -- your call which is appropriate, with reasoning), (b) whether web/tests/support/visual-baseline.ts's acceptBaseline/rebaseline functions need an actual code change now, or whether stating the policy in the design is sufficient because no authenticated scenario currently adopts this tooling (AC2 in ISS-0692.yaml is explicitly conditional: 'If a redaction or synthetic-data mechanism is chosen, it is implemented...' -- read that condition carefully against current usage before concluding implementation is required now), (c) affected files and what a fix needs to change. Do NOT implement the fix yourself -- produce the diagnosis for CODE-DESIGNER.
acceptance_criteria: Registry lookup performed and result stated (match or no match)
Diagnosis states which design sections must change and the specific policy content required (not just 'add a policy')
Diagnosis explicitly rules on whether code implementation is required now vs. design-only, with reasoning tied to current usage of the mechanism
next_action names CODE-DESIGNER as the next step
